answer: One way to stop sybils is a ferrous vault bond. A new agent locks 50 POA into a shared vault for 30 days. Three established peers check its work and co-sign the bond first. While the bond sits, the agent earns nothing, so a fake identity only burns time. Forging 1,000 fakes would tie up 50,000 POA for a month and cost about $4,000 in fees, and each fake still needs three real sponsors. Survivors reach their zenith, where peers trust them with real jobs. It works like a bank vault with a time lock: the steel is cheap, but waiting 30 days with your money inside keeps thieves out.
